papers.title: Dissecting the genetic architecture for maize prolificacy by combining QTL mapping and genome-wide association study.
papers.abstract: Maize prolificacy (ears per plant) is a vital domestication trait in maize that profoundly determines grain yield potential. Deciphering its genetic regulatory network is essential for improving yield performance and expanding germplasm diversity. Here, we performed multi-environment phenotypic evaluation on two RIL populations and one association panel. Integrative QTL mapping and GWAS uncovered 13 QTLs and 8 QTNs associated with maize prolificacy. The stable locus qP9-2 harbored two tissue differentiation-associated genes (Zm00001eb395530, Zm00001eb395480), while the significant SNPs within
papers.journal: Molecular breeding : new strategies in plant improvement
papers.summary: This study dissects the genetic basis of maize prolificacy (number of ears per plant) by combining QTL mapping in two recombinant inbred line populations with genome-wide association study in an association panel across multiple environments. The authors identify 13 QTLs and 8 quantitative trait nucleotides, including a stable locus (qP9-2) containing two candidate genes linked to tissue differentiation. These findings provide genetic targets and a regulatory framework for improving maize yield potential through breeding.

papers.title: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing reveals the 2'-O-methylation landscape and SNORD88B-guided FN1 modification in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To systematically map the internal 2'-O-methylation (Nm) landscape on messenger RNA (mRNA) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), characterize its distribution features and biological functions, and identify key C/D box small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs) that regulate Nm modification along with their target genes, thereby providing a molecular basis for elucidating post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms in HCC.
papers.summary: This study uses nanopore direct RNA sequencing to map the internal 2'-O-methylation (Nm) landscape on mRNA in hepatocellular carcinoma, characterizing its distribution and biological functions. The authors identify C/D box snoRNAs, particularly SNORD88B, that guide Nm modification of the FN1 gene, providing a molecular basis for post-transcriptional regulation in HCC.

papers.title: DNA methylation signatures from tissue and cell-free DNA in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency mirror clinical pathologies providing a potential non-invasive tool to monitor liver disease progression.
papers.abstract: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is a serpinopathy in which mutations in the SERPINA1 gene cause misfolding of alpha-1 antitrypsin (Z-AAT), leading to hepatic protein accumulation, proteotoxic stress, inflammation, fibrosis, and an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma. Despite a uniform genetic mutation in most affected individuals, liver disease severity varies, reflecting contributions from environmental exposures and epigenetic heterogeneity (e.g. DNA methylation). As RNA-interference therapy has emerged as a promising treatment, understanding how epigenetic variation relates to
papers.summary: This study examines DNA methylation patterns in both liver tissue and cell-free DNA from patients with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, finding that these epigenetic signatures reflect the clinical pathologies associated with the disease, including liver damage and fibrosis. The authors propose that cell-free DNA methylation could serve as a non-invasive biomarker to monitor liver disease progression in AATD patients, which is important given the variable severity of liver disease despite uniform genetic mutations.

papers.title: MaxGeomHash bridges MinHash and FracMinHash for scalable similarity estimation using sub-linear k-mer sketching.
papers.abstract: With the surge in sequencing data generated from biological studies, designing scalable computational techniques has become essential. One effective strategy to enable large-scale computation is to extract k-mers from long sequences, and summarize large k-mer sets into random samples (a.k.a. sketches). These sketches enable rapid estimation of similarity metrics such as Jaccard or cosine, and thus facilitate scalable computations. Popular sketching tools in bioinformatics range from the MinHash algorithm to generate fixed-size sketches; to FracMinHash algorithm to retain a fraction of all k-me
papers.summary: The paper introduces MaxGeomHash, a new sketching method that combines ideas from MinHash (fixed-size sketches) and FracMinHash (fraction-based sampling) to estimate k-mer set similarity more scalably. By using sub-linear k-mer sketching, it aims to reduce computational and memory costs while maintaining accurate Jaccard/cosine similarity estimates for large sequencing datasets. This bridges two popular sketching paradigms and offers a practical tool for large-scale genomic comparisons.

papers.title: Genomic and biological characterization of exopolysaccharides produced by Streptococcus thermophilus CCASU-ST-S3 and CCASU-ST-S52, with statistical optimization and preliminary spectroscopic characterization of EPS-STS3.
papers.abstract: Streptococcus thermophilus is a key dairy starter capable of producing exopolysaccharides (EPS) with strain-dependent biosynthetic and biological properties. Two EPS-producing strains, STS3 and STS52, isolated from yogurt, were characterized genomically, and their partially purified EPS preparations underwent preliminary biological evaluation.
papers.summary: This study genomically characterized two yogurt-derived Streptococcus thermophilus strains (STS3 and STS52) that produce exopolysaccharides, and statistically optimized EPS production for STS3 with preliminary spectroscopic characterization. The work links strain-specific genomic features to EPS biosynthetic capacity and reports preliminary biological evaluation of the partially purified EPS preparations.

papers.title: ABAQS: A comprehensive scoring method for assessing genome annotation quality.
papers.abstract: As genome resources continue to expand, estimating the accuracy and completeness of genome annotations (e.g., gene and protein models) becomes essential to ensure quality of downstream analyses and applications. It becomes critical in comparative genomic analysis to select genomes with comparable qualities of assembly and annotation. Without careful scrutiny, inconsistencies in annotation quality can undermine downstream studies.
papers.summary: ABAQS introduces a comprehensive scoring method for assessing the quality and completeness of genome annotations, including gene and protein models. The approach helps researchers compare annotation quality across genomes, which is critical for ensuring reliable downstream comparative genomic analyses.

papers.title: Chromatin compartment shifting is recurrent and associated with epigenetic reprogramming in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional chromatin organization shapes gene regulation by partitioning the genome into transcriptionally active and inactive compartments, with implications for prostate carcinogenesis. We integrated Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical samples representing benign prostatic hyperplasia, primary prostate cancer (PC), and castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). Using a computational framework accounting for copy number variation and tumor purity, we characterized A/B chromatin compartment organization in aneuploid tumors. We identified recurrent shifts from inac
papers.summary: This study integrated Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical prostate samples to map A/B chromatin compartments across benign, primary, and castration-resistant prostate cancer. The authors developed a computational framework that accounts for copy number variation and tumor purity, revealing recurrent shifts from inactive (B) to active (A) compartments in aneuploid tumors. These compartment changes are associated with epigenetic reprogramming, suggesting that 3D genome reorganization contributes to prostate cancer progression.

papers.title: hlafactor: a tool for multi-layer functional annotation of HLA variation.
papers.abstract: The human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system is the most polymorphic region of the human genome and a major determinant of immune function and disease susceptibility. Ideally, analyses of HLA variation would capture multiple layers of information, from classical alleles and amino-acid residues to higher-level functional properties such as tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups. However, while allele- and amino-acid-level data are now routinely available, the corresponding functional annotations remain scattered across publications and reference datasets, and no exis
papers.summary: hlafactor is a new software tool that consolidates multiple layers of HLA functional annotation—classical alleles, amino-acid residues, and higher-level properties like tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups—into a single resource. It addresses the fragmentation of HLA functional data across publications and reference datasets, enabling integrated multi-layer analyses of this highly polymorphic immune region.

papers.title: DGIdb in 2026: an interoperable resource for the druggable genome.
papers.abstract: The Drug-Gene Interaction Database (DGIdb; https://dgidb.org) is an open-access aggregate knowledgebase that normalizes and centralizes drug-gene interaction and gene annotation data from diverse therapeutic and biomedical sources. Since its previous update, DGIdb has expanded its data content and added new tooling to better support programmatic access and local deployment. This release updates existing sources and incorporates three new sources of interaction data, including annotation data from the Molecular Oncology Almanac, the PRISM Repurposing Dataset, and the Broad Institute Drug Repurp
papers.summary: DGIdb 2026 is an updated open-access knowledgebase that aggregates and normalizes drug-gene interaction and gene annotation data from many sources. This release adds three new interaction data sources (Molecular Oncology Almanac, PRISM Repurposing Dataset, and Broad Institute Drug Repurposing data) and introduces new tooling for programmatic access and local deployment. It serves as an interoperable resource for druggable genome research.

papers.title: Beyond Mutations: A Seven-CpG DNA Methylation Signature for Predicting HRD in MMRd Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: We previously identified a high level of molecular heterogeneity within mismatch repair deficiency (MMRd) colorectal cancer (CRC). Despite MMRd CRC being typically considered suitable for immunotherapy, only less than half of the metastatic CRC (mCRC) patients achieve complete remission. Thus, the search for identifying new therapeutic targets has become extremely urgent. The use of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi) has revolutionized the treatment of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) cancer; however, the HRD prevalence in CRC remains unclear. Here, we conducted an integra
papers.summary: This study identifies a seven-CpG DNA methylation signature that can predict homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) in mismatch repair-deficient colorectal cancer, going beyond mutation-based detection. The authors integrate methylation data to capture molecular heterogeneity within MMRd CRC, aiming to identify patients who might benefit from PARP inhibitors. The signature offers a potential epigenetic biomarker for expanding targeted therapy options in this subset of colorectal cancer.

papers.title: Multi-centre implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome test for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Low-coverage whole-genome sequencing offers a scalable approach to homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) testing in ovarian cancer. This multi-centre study describes the real-world implementation of one such assay, SeqOne SomaHRD, across four European laboratories between 9 January 2023 and 1 October 2025. Tumours were classified as HRD-positive if they had a Genomic Instability score (GIS) of ≥0.50 (GIS-high) and/or a pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant. GIS was generated from two bioinformatically derived measures of genomic instability: Large-scale Genomic Alterations (LGA) and Loss of Parental
papers.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
papers.summary: This multi-centre study reports real-world implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome sequencing assay (SeqOne SomaHRD) for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer across four European laboratories. Tumours were classified as HRD-positive based on a Genomic Instability score threshold and/or pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants, with the score derived from bioinformatic measures of large-scale genomic alterations and loss of heterozygosity. The work demonstrates that low-coverage WGS can be deployed as a scalable, practical HRD testing approach in routine clinical settings.

papers.title: DeGenRESOLVE: An offline GUI-based automated nanopore sequencing pipeline for viruses with custom rule-based indel and degeneracy resolution.
papers.abstract: Sequencing methods based on Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) have revolutionized the field of viral genomics. However, available analysis tools are often internet-dependent, have complex installation requirements, or lack graphical user interfaces (GUIs), limiting their use in laboratories with restricted internet access or limited bioinformatics expertise. Here we present DeGenRESOLVE, a pipeline designed for amplicon-based ONT resequencing where a reference genome is available. This pipeline does not perform de novo assembly but processes raw base-called ONT viral sequencing data offline i
papers.summary: DeGenRESOLVE is an offline, GUI-based pipeline for analyzing amplicon-based Oxford Nanopore sequencing data from viruses when a reference genome is available. It automates the workflow and includes custom rule-based resolution of indels and degenerate bases, addressing the need for tools that work without internet access or advanced bioinformatics skills. The tool is aimed at laboratories with limited connectivity or expertise.

papers.title: Epigenome-informed prioritization of bivalent chromatin SNPs enhances genomic prediction robustness: a proof-of-concept study in Pacific white shrimp ( Litopenaeus vannamei).
papers.abstract: Genomic selection has become a powerful tool for accelerating genetic improvement in animal breeding, yet its broader application is often limited by high genotyping costs and reduced predictive reliability across populations. Functional genomic annotations offer a promising strategy to prioritize biologically meaningful variants and improve prediction robustness. Here, using Pacific white shrimp ( Litopenaeus vannamei) as a model, we conducted a proof-of-concept study integrating whole-genome resequencing and phenotypic data from 972 individuals. High-resolution epigenomic maps were generated
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study in Pacific white shrimp integrates whole-genome resequencing, phenotypic data from 972 individuals, and high-resolution epigenomic maps to prioritize SNPs located in bivalent chromatin regions for genomic selection. The authors show that epigenome-informed SNP prioritization can improve the robustness of genomic prediction while potentially reducing genotyping costs. The work demonstrates how functional genomic annotations can enhance animal breeding programs.

papers.title: Bridging BET bromodomain and immune checkpoint inhibitors through generative bioorganic frameworks for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Bromodomain and extraterminal domain (BET) proteins are epigenetic readers that couple chromatin acetylation to oncogenic and immune-regulatory gene transcription, making them attractive targets for combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in precision oncology. This review synthesizes current mechanistic, medicinal-chemistry, and translational evidence on BET-ICI combination strategies. We describe how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, thereby increasing tumor susceptibility to immune-mediated attack
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic and medicinal-chemistry evidence on combining BET bromodomain inhibitors with immune checkpoint inhibitors for cancer therapy. It describes how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, increasing tumor susceptibility to immune attack. The authors frame generative bioorganic approaches as a route to next-generation combination agents.

papers.title: Auditing the adversarial robustness of genomic foundation models with SafeGenes.
papers.abstract: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) such as evolutionary scale modeling (ESM) are increasingly applied to variant effect prediction in clinical genomics, yet their adversarial robustness remains underexplored. We present SafeGenes, an evaluation framework combining input-space attacks, a discrete single-nucleotide variant (SNV)-reachable HotFlip attack, and a soft-prompt-triggered backdoor. Across cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia datasets, iterative attacks severely degrade discrimination: projected gradient descent (PGD) reduces the area under the curve (AUC) by more than 30 percentage points, and
papers.summary: SafeGenes is an evaluation framework that tests how easily genomic foundation models (like ESM) can be fooled by adversarial perturbations when predicting variant effects. Using input-space attacks, a discrete SNV-reachable HotFlip attack, and a soft-prompt backdoor, the authors show that iterative attacks such as PGD can drop AUC by over 30 percentage points on cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia datasets. This highlights a serious robustness gap for clinical genomics applications built on GFMs.

papers.title: Computational and experimental strategies for functional validation of non-coding variants in pancreatic cancer.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterised by extensive genomic heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Although recurrent coding mutations in key driver genes have been well researched, large-scale sequencing studies have identified a broad array of non-coding variants which may contribute to tumorigenesis by interfering with gene regulatory mechanisms. However, understanding the functional significance of these variants remains a major challenge due to their abundance and the complexity of non-coding regulatory structures. This review outli
papers.summary: This review discusses computational and experimental approaches for functionally validating non-coding genetic variants in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). It highlights the challenge of interpreting the many non-coding variants identified by sequencing studies and outlines strategies to determine which ones affect gene regulation and contribute to tumorigenesis.

papers.title: MARiO: Predicting Cancer Variant Pathogenicity by Integrating In Silico Evaluation and Patient-Level Mutational Contexts.
papers.abstract: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) supports precision medicine in cancer care, but accurate assessment of missense variant pathogenicity, especially for variants without established consensus, remains challenging. Various computational tools have been developed for variant functional prediction, but most current tools rely solely on variant-level features and do not capture the clinical context of individual patients. To address this limitation, we developed MARiO (Missense Alteration Risk identifier in Oncology), a machine-learning model that integrates variant-level features and patient-l
papers.summary: MARiO is a machine-learning model that predicts the pathogenicity of missense cancer variants by combining variant-level in silico features with patient-level mutational context, addressing the limitation of tools that ignore clinical context. This integration aims to improve variant interpretation in comprehensive genomic profiling for precision oncology, particularly for variants lacking established consensus.

papers.title: Pooled multiplex amplicon massive parallel sequencing for high-throughput confirmation of whole-genome sequencing potentially pathogenic variants in patients with parkinsonism.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) identifies large numbers of genetic variants, although only a subset requires independent confirmation for clinical interpretation. Sanger sequencing remains the standard confirmation method but is impractical for large-scale variant verification. We developed and evaluated a strategy for variant confirmation based on multi-amplicon massively parallel sequencing of pooled DNA samples. WGS data were obtained from 86 individuals, including patients with parkinsonism and controls. Variants were selected using phenotype-driven filtering, ClinVar classification, and pa
papers.summary: The authors developed a pooled multiplex amplicon massively parallel sequencing strategy to confirm potentially pathogenic variants identified by whole-genome sequencing in patients with parkinsonism. This approach enables high-throughput validation of many variants across multiple samples in a single sequencing run, offering a scalable alternative to Sanger sequencing. The method was evaluated on 86 individuals, demonstrating feasibility for large-scale clinical variant confirmation.

papers.title: H3K9 demethylase KDM3A potentiates interferon signaling and macrophage-driven inflammation in atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Macrophages drive atherosclerosis through inflammatory activation programs shaped by metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. H3K9 methylation enforces heterochromatin states and represses transcription, whereas removal of this histone modification creates transcriptionally permissive chromatin. Here, we identified KDM3A-mediated H3K9 demethylation to enhance chromatin accessibility at interferon (IFN) signaling loci, thereby promoting IFN production and downstream IFN-dependent transcriptional and chemokine responses. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, hematopoietic Kdm3a deficiency reduces
papers.summary: This study shows that the histone demethylase KDM3A removes H3K9 methylation at interferon signaling loci in macrophages, opening chromatin and boosting interferon production and downstream inflammatory chemokine responses. In a mouse atherosclerosis model, deleting Kdm3a in blood cells reduced this inflammatory program, implicating KDM3A as an epigenetic driver of macrophage-driven plaque inflammation.

papers.title: Genome-Guided Discovery of ShK-like Peptides from Sanderia malayensis with Anti-Amyloidogenic and Neuroprotective Activities.
papers.abstract: While jellyfish venom represents a promising bioresource for biotechnological applications, the extraction of adequate venom amounts and the isolation of pure toxins present significant technical bottlenecks. To overcome these difficulties, a pipeline utilizing bioinformatic analyses was established to identify toxin candidates from genomic datasets, subsequently validating their functions from chemical synthesis. Specifically, a high-quality, 144 Mb genome assembly of the jellyfish Sanderia malayensis was constructed using PacBio CLR long reads (38.2 Gb), Illumina short reads (24.5 Gb), and H
papers.summary: The authors assembled a high-quality 144 Mb genome of the jellyfish Sanderia malayensis and used bioinformatic mining to identify ShK-like toxin peptides, which they then produced by chemical synthesis and tested functionally. The synthesized peptides showed anti-amyloidogenic and neuroprotective activities, demonstrating that genome-guided discovery can bypass the technical bottlenecks of venom extraction and toxin isolation.

papers.title: Detection of Maximal Exact Matches in Terabases of Genome Assemblies in Compressed Space and Sublinear Time.
papers.abstract: Detection of long exact matches between a pair of genomes has historically been a fundamental operation in genomics. Similarly, detection of long exact matches between all pairs of haplotypes in a large panel of genotyping array data or whole-genome sequencing variant calls is a fundamental operation in population genetics. Thanks to various recent pangenome efforts, for the first time, large panels of high-quality genome assemblies are being constructed. Therefore, we propose the intersection of these two approaches: detection of long exact matches between all pairs of assemblies in panels of
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper introduces a method for detecting maximal exact matches (MEMs) between all pairs of genome assemblies in large panels, operating directly on compressed data and in sublinear time. This enables scalable comparative genomics across terabase-scale assembly collections, which is increasingly relevant as pangenome projects generate many high-quality haplotypes.

papers.title: Disease-modifying therapies in development for post-traumatic epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) is a chronic neurological disorder that develops following traumatic brain injury (TBI), a condition affecting nearly 69 million people worldwide. PTE accounts for 20% of acquired epilepsies and is characterized by spontaneous recurrent seizures and long-term neurological deficits. Current antiseizure medications primarily suppress early seizures but do not prevent epileptogenesis or improve long-term neurological dysfunction. This review critically evaluates the current landscape of disease-modifying therapies for PTE with an emphasis on pathophysiological basis,
papers.summary: This review evaluates emerging disease-modifying therapies for post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE), a condition affecting 20% of acquired epilepsies that currently lacks treatments to prevent epileptogenesis or long-term neurological deficits. The authors critically assess the pathophysiological basis of PTE and the current landscape of candidate therapies aimed at modifying disease progression rather than merely suppressing seizures.

papers.title: Accelerating discovery and integration from RNA to Protein with R2T2P.
papers.abstract: Integrating transcriptomics and proteomics data remains an unmet challenge in the post-genomics era, discouraging researchers from pursuing integrative approaches to molecular biology research. Leveraging the power of translation profiling, we present RNA to Translation to Protein (R2T2P), a computational platform integrating genome-guided transcriptome assembly with identification of translation and proteins, including a tailored differential analysis framework and support for multiple reference transcriptomes. We applied R2T2P to investigate a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular d
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: R2T2P is a new computational platform that integrates transcriptomics and proteomics data by leveraging translation profiling, combining genome-guided transcriptome assembly with identification of translated sequences and proteins. It includes a tailored differential analysis framework and supports multiple reference transcriptomes. The authors applied it to a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy, demonstrating its utility for integrative molecular analysis.

papers.title: Multi-omics approaches to unravel the biological effects of DNA-binding small molecules.
papers.abstract: DNA-targeting ligands comprise a diverse class of molecules that bind either canonical duplex DNA or non-canonical DNA structures such as G-quadruplexes. The recent shift towards combining distinct omics approaches, including epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, is significantly expanding the understanding of the biological effects induced by these small molecules, capturing complex cellular perturbations across multiple molecular layers. Here, we report representative examples from recent literature that illustrate how multi-omics approaches have helped to uncover previ
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining multiple omics approaches (epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics) is expanding our understanding of how DNA-binding small molecules affect cells. The authors highlight recent examples showing that multi-omics can capture complex cellular perturbations across molecular layers, revealing effects that single-omics studies would miss.

papers.title: A multi-scale cell-type resolved map of trans -regulatory architecture in the aging human brain.
papers.abstract: Mapping genetic effects on distal genes and regulatory programs is essential for understanding how genetic variation influences complex diseases; yet trans -QTL discovery remains limited by weak effect sizes, extensive multiple testing and poor reproducibility. Here, we introduce TransMap , a generalizable computational framework that combines multi-scale trans -QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve the discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Beyond individual trans -eGenes, TransMap constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes that account
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: TransMap is a computational framework that improves detection of trans-QTLs—genetic variants that affect distant genes—by combining multi-scale mapping with multi-phenotype colocalization. Applied to the aging human brain at cell-type resolution, it constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes to boost discovery and interpretability of distal regulatory variants. This provides a more reproducible map of trans-regulatory architecture relevant to brain aging and complex disease.

papers.title: Epigenetic profiling of neuroactive curcumin on histone signatures in breast cancer using gen3DNet.
papers.abstract: Aberrant epigenetic alterations are implicated in the transformation of normal cells into cancerous ones. Unlike genetic mutations, these dysregulations can be reversible and are potential targets for anticancer drugs. Curcumin, a natural plant-derived compound, has been shown to have anticancer effects and neuroprotective properties via its influence on epigenetic regulation. However, the precise nature of these epigenetic changes and the mechanisms driving them remain largely unexplored. Moreover, there is strong evidence linking the neuroactive properties of chemotherapy drugs in the treatm
papers.summary: This study uses a computational approach called gen3DNet to profile how curcumin, a plant-derived compound with anticancer and neuroactive properties, alters histone epigenetic signatures in breast cancer cells. The work aims to clarify the reversible epigenetic changes induced by curcumin, which could inform its use as an anticancer agent and shed light on neurological side effects of chemotherapy.

papers.title: Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Bioinformatics analyses were conducted using publicly available HCC transcriptomic datasets from GEO database, disease gene database (GeneCards database), and chemical-gene interaction networks (Comparative Toxicogenomic Database) to identify potential therapeutic targets, HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key therapeutic ta
papers.summary: This study combines bioinformatics analysis of public HCC transcriptomic datasets with in vitro experiments to show that sodium propionate, a short-chain fatty acid, suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma cell growth by downregulating the histone deacetylases HDAC2 and HDAC6. The work positions SP as a potential epigenetic modulator for HCC, though the evidence is largely correlative and preliminary.

papers.title: A Batch-Processing Pipeline for RNA-seq Gene Abundance Estimation.
papers.abstract: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets provide valuable opportunities to investigate gene and transcript abundance across species, tissues, developmental stages, and experimental conditions. However, processing multiple datasets consistently remains challenging because sequencing runs may differ in library layout, read length, sequencing depth, metadata quality, and analytical settings. Existing RNA-seq workflows often depend on dedicated workflow managers, substantial computational infrastructure, or advanced bioinformatics expertise, which may limit their accessibility for routine analyses. We pr
papers.summary: This paper presents a batch-processing pipeline for estimating gene abundance from RNA-seq data. It addresses the challenge of consistently processing multiple datasets that differ in library layout, read length, sequencing depth, and metadata quality, while avoiding dependence on dedicated workflow managers or advanced bioinformatics expertise. The pipeline aims to make routine RNA-seq analyses more accessible.

papers.title: Co-mutation of KRAS and ARID1A correlates with the MSI/LINE-1 hypermethylation profile in endometrial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The interaction between oncogenic signalling and epigenetics in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma (EEC) is poorly defined. We investigated the potential association of KRAS-ARID1A co-mutation axis with a distinct hypermethylator phenotype, affecting focal MLH1 promoter methylation and global DNA methylation (LINE-1).
papers.summary: This study examines whether co-occurring mutations in KRAS and ARID1A define a distinct epigenetic subtype in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma. The authors find that KRAS-ARID1A co-mutation is associated with a hypermethylator phenotype, including focal MLH1 promoter methylation and altered global LINE-1 methylation. This links oncogenic signalling to epigenetic dysregulation and may help stratify endometrial cancers by molecular profile.

papers.title: CALB1 expression in meningioma: associations with progression-free survival and chromosome arm 6q loss.
papers.abstract: Molecular profiling has refined risk stratification in meningioma, but the biological relevance of associated transcriptional changes remains incompletely understood. Calbindin D28K (Calb), encoded by CALB1, is a calcium-binding protein with reported anti-apoptotic and cytoprotective functions. Previous unsupervised transcriptomic analysis identified CALB1 upregulation in meningiomas with aggressive cellular features, but its biological and clinical relevance remains unresolved. We analysed Calb immunoreactivity in 231 meningioma tissue microarray (TMA) cores from 147 patients and evaluated CA
papers.summary: This study examined calbindin D28K (CALB1) protein expression in 231 meningioma tissue samples from 147 patients, finding that higher CALB1 immunoreactivity is associated with progression-free survival and with loss of chromosome arm 6q. The work links a transcriptional marker of aggressive meningioma biology to a specific chromosomal alteration, suggesting CALB1 may help refine risk stratification.

papers.title: gcat, its_a_scam: modular tools for single cell data processing and per-cell quality control.
papers.abstract: The era of designing bioinformatic pipelines using open source tools is giving way to monolithic, and often proprietary, tools designed for end-to-end analysis, especially in the context of single cell data. While these tools are convenient for going from sequencing data to an almost complete data analysis "in a few clicks", they can strongly limit data use beyond standard analyses.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present gcat and its_a_scam, two modular open-source tools for single-cell data processing and per-cell quality control. These tools aim to counter the trend toward monolithic, often proprietary, end-to-end pipelines by keeping analysis steps composable and data accessible for non-standard downstream use.

papers.title: Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes.
papers.abstract: Plateau aquatic environments expose fishes to chronic cold, hypoxia, ultraviolet radiation and low productivity, providing natural systems for studying genomic features associated with environmental adaptation. Whether related fishes inhabiting similar cold-water plateau environments exhibit comparable or divergent genomic responses remains unclear. We compared two plateau cypriniform fishes, Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus, within a 12-species phylogenomic framework, integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, chromosome-scale synteny and
papers.summary: This study compares the genomes of two ecologically similar plateau fishes, Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus, within a 12-species phylogenomic framework to ask whether related fishes in similar cold-water plateau environments show convergent or divergent genomic adaptations. By integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, and chromosome-scale synteny, the authors find contrasting candidate adaptive signatures between the two species, suggesting that similar environmental pressures can elicit divergent genomic responses even among closely related fishes.

papers.title: Topological Data Analysis Identifies Copy Number Variation Subtypes of Bulls Associated with Fertility.
papers.abstract: Bull fertility is a polygenic trait of significant economic importance in dairy and beef cattle, controlled by multiple genetic variants, including copy number variations (CNVs). Conventional single-variant association analyses primarily evaluate marginal effects of individual loci, whereas CNV co-occurrence patterns require complementary approaches. This study applied topological data analysis (TDA) to identify groups of bulls based on genome-wide CNVR profiles and to assess their association with insemination success rate. A total of 88 bulls were included, and the presence/absence of 406 co
papers.summary: This study applied topological data analysis (TDA) to genome-wide copy number variation (CNV) profiles from 88 bulls, grouping animals by CNV co-occurrence patterns rather than single-locus effects. The resulting CNV-based subgroups were associated with insemination success rate, suggesting that combined CNV signatures—not just individual variants—relate to bull fertility. The work demonstrates a complementary, pattern-based approach for a polygenic trait of economic importance in cattle breeding.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer: from carcinogenesis and molecular classification to targeted therapy.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a heterogeneous disease that results from the progressive accumulation and interactions at multiple levels of genetic alterations, which lead to the transformation of normal colonic epithelium into malignant colorectal tumors. Understanding the molecular basis of CRC pathogenesis, together with the interactions between genetic alterations, epigenetic modifications, environmental and lifestyle factors, is essential for improving prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment strategies. This review aims to provide a critical reference point for understanding the temp
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the molecular mechanisms underlying colorectal cancer, covering the progressive accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations that drive transformation of normal colonic epithelium into malignancy. It discusses molecular classification schemes and how these inform targeted therapy strategies, emphasizing interactions between genetic changes, epigenetic modifications, and environmental/lifestyle factors. The work serves as a critical reference for understanding CRC pathogenesis and improving prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment.

papers.title: Variant Classification of a Non-Protein Coding Gene: ACMG/AMP Specifications for RMRP from the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel.
papers.abstract: This study, conducted by the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel (ClinGen SCID-VCEP), aimed to adapt the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) framework for germline variant interpretation in RMRP . Unlike the protein-coding genes for which the framework was primarily developed, RMRP encodes a non-protein-coding RNA. Biallelic pathogenic variants in RMRP cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia, which can include severe combined immunodeficiency disease and other immune abnormalities.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This paper presents expert-panel specifications for applying the ACMG/AMP variant classification framework to RMRP, a non-protein-coding RNA gene where biallelic pathogenic variants cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia and associated immunodeficiency. Because the standard framework was designed for protein-coding genes, the ClinGen SCID Variant Curation Expert Panel adapted criteria to account for the gene's non-coding nature, providing standardized guidance for clinical interpretation of RMRP variants.

papers.title: Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.
papers.abstract: Histone posttranslational modifications, particularly lysine acetylation (Kac), are critical epigenetic regulators of transcriptional programs underlying long-term memory consolidation. Beyond Kac, several other non-acetyl acylations have been identified with the ability to regulate transcription; however, their role in memory consolidation remains unknown. Here, we identify histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a molecular switch for long-term memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. We find that spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study identifies histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr), a non-acetyl histone modification, as a key epigenetic switch controlling long-term spatial memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. Spatial learning produces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions, suggesting Kcr regulates the transcriptional programs needed for memory consolidation beyond the well-studied role of histone acetylation.

papers.title: Systematic benchmarking of Hi-C-based scaffolding methods in genome assembly.
papers.abstract: High-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) technology is crucial for scaffolding, a key step to generate chromosome-level high-quality genome assemblies. However, although several Hi-C-based scaffolding tools have been developed, their utility in genome assembly remains constrained by inconsistent performance, making a systematic benchmarking urgently needed. Here, we present a comprehensive benchmark of five prominent Hi-C scaffolders using simulated contig assemblies considering various factors, including contig lengths, chimeric contig proportions, Hi-C coverage depths, and ploi
papers.summary: This paper systematically benchmarks five popular Hi-C-based scaffolding tools across simulated contig assemblies, varying contig length, chimeric contig proportion, Hi-C coverage depth, and ploidy. It identifies how these factors affect scaffolding accuracy and completeness, providing practical guidance on tool selection and parameter settings for chromosome-level genome assembly.

papers.title: Correction of the cytosine deamination artifacts in FFPE-based sequencing experiments.
papers.abstract: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues remain an essential resource for molecular studies, yet formalin-induced cytosine deamination introduces characteristic C > T/G > A artifacts that compromise the accuracy of next-generation sequencing analyses. Numerous computational methods and enzymatic DNA repair strategies have been proposed to reduce these artifacts, but no systematic comparison across tools and experimental conditions exists. Here, we evaluate the performance of seven computational approaches (SOBDetector, Ideafix, MicroSEC, FFPolish, DeepOmics FFPE/FFPE-PLUS, FFPErase) to
papers.summary: This paper systematically benchmarks seven computational tools (SOBDetector, Ideafix, MicroSEC, FFPolish, DeepOmics FFPE/FFPE-PLUS, FFPErase) for correcting cytosine deamination artifacts (C>T/G>A) in FFPE tissue sequencing data. It provides the first cross-tool comparison under varied experimental conditions, helping researchers choose appropriate correction methods for their FFPE studies.

papers.title: XenoMix: estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation microarrays enable cost-effective, high-throughput profiling of human and mouse samples and are widely used to study epigenetic alterations in cancer. Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models complement this approach by preserving primary tumor characteristics while enabling in vivo studies of drug response and therapy resistance. However, it remains difficult to quantify mouse DNA contamination in PDX DNA methylation data generated using microarrays. We present XenoMix, a light-weight computational tool for quantifying mouse DNA contamination directly from DNA methylation data i
papers.summary: XenoMix is a lightweight computational tool that estimates the proportion of mouse DNA contamination in Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) DNA methylation microarray data. It addresses the common problem of mixed human-mouse signal in PDX epigenomic profiling, enabling researchers to quantify and account for contamination without additional experimental steps.

papers.title: quarTeT after 3 years: toolkit updates and community insights for telomere-to-telomere genome assembly.
papers.abstract: Since its initial release in 2023, quarTeT has become a widely used toolkit for telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly and characterization. Here, we present a major update that improves all four quarTeT modules, including optional contig filtering in AssemblyMapper, a refactored join algorithm in GapFiller, enhanced telomere detection in TeloExplorer (TE), and support for holocentric chromosomes in CentroMiner (CM). The main program has also been upgraded with user-configurable multithreading, broader version compatibility, and simplified deployment via Bioconda, Docker, and Singularity.
papers.summary: This paper describes a major update to quarTeT, a widely used toolkit for telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly and characterization. The update improves all four modules—AssemblyMapper, GapFiller, TeloExplorer, and CentroMiner—adding features like optional contig filtering, a refactored join algorithm, enhanced telomere detection, and support for holocentric chromosomes, plus user-configurable multithreading and easier deployment via Bioconda, Docker, and Singularity.

papers.title: MLMP: A Methylation-Associated lncRNA-mRNA Prognostic Signature for Endometrial Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is one of the most common gynecological malignancies. Aberrant DNA methylation (DNAm) is an important epigenetic alteration involved in cancer progression. Long non-coding RNAs (LncRNAs) play critical roles in gene regulation and pathological processes. However, the biological and prognostic significance of lncRNA-mRNA pairs associated with methylation remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study develops MLMP, a prognostic signature for endometrial carcinoma built from methylation-associated lncRNA-mRNA pairs. The authors identify DNA methylation-linked lncRNA-mRNA interactions and combine them into a model intended to predict patient outcomes. The work extends epigenetic and transcriptomic biomarker approaches to EC prognosis.

papers.title: Epigenetic Insights in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis: DNA Methylation Highlights an Involvement of Epstein-Barr Virus Infection and Host Immune Networks.
papers.abstract: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) provides a unique opportunity to investigate MS pathogenesis because of the short interval between environmental exposures and disease onset. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that mediate the interplay between environmental triggers and genomic factors in the early stages of the disease.
papers.summary: This study identifies differentially methylated DNA regions in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis, a form of MS with a short interval between environmental exposure and disease onset. The methylation changes point to Epstein-Barr virus infection and host immune networks as key players in early disease pathogenesis.

papers.title: MethyAnno: An Interpretable Automated Annotation Method Leveraging Multi-Scale Information and Metric Learning Framework for scDNAm Data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) sequencing provides unique insights into epigenetic heterogeneity and cell-specific regulatory landscapes. However, accurate cell type annotation for scDNAm data remains challenging, as the distinct data distribution of scDNAm hinders the adaptation of annotation methods from other omics, and specialized annotation tools for scDNAm are currently lacking. Here, MethyAnno is proposed as an interpretable deep metric learning framework that leverages multi-scale information for accurate cell type annotation of scDNAm data. Additionally, MethyAnno enables genera
papers.summary: MethyAnno is a new interpretable deep metric learning framework that annotates cell types in single-cell DNA methylation data by combining multi-scale information. It addresses the lack of specialized annotation tools for scDNAm, whose distinct data distribution makes methods from other omics ineffective. The method also supports downstream analyses such as generalization across datasets.

papers.title: Assessing the predictive potential of the Holstein bovine sperm methylome for bull fertility using machine learning.
papers.abstract: Bull fertility is a key parameter in the dairy cattle industry, with significant economic implications. DNA methylation is an epigenetic mark essential for fertility, and recent works have highlighted sperm DNA methylation as a promising source of biomarkers for male fertility, but no operational tool has been developed for predicting bull fertility based on DNA methylation. Here, we leveraged existing methylation data to evaluate the potential of DNA methylation for predicting bull fertility with machine learning models.
papers.summary: This study evaluated whether DNA methylation patterns in Holstein bull sperm can predict bull fertility using machine learning models. Leveraging existing methylation data, the authors assessed the predictive potential of sperm methylome biomarkers for male fertility in dairy cattle. The work represents a step toward developing operational tools for fertility prediction based on epigenetic marks.

papers.title: Gestational Pyrethroid Exposure and Placental Health in Wistar Rats: Evaluation of Epigenetic, Developmental, and Oxidative Stress Biomarkers.
papers.abstract: Understanding the mechanisms of placental toxicity provides an important research tool that can help to clarify how early-life exposure may influence adverse pregnancy outcomes, foetal health, and long-term disease risk in adulthood. In the present study we estimated the effects of oral gestational exposure to the pyrethroid insecticide α-cypermethrin (α-cyp), a potential endocrine disruptor, in doses of 1, 10, and 19 mg/kg bw/day on different parameters in placentas of Wistar rats (n = 5 per group; 30 animals in total). We evaluated global DNA methylation within the LINE1 repetitive region us
papers.summary: This study examined how gestational exposure to the pyrethroid insecticide α-cypermethrin affects placental health in Wistar rats, testing three dose levels. The researchers measured global DNA methylation in the LINE1 repetitive region alongside developmental and oxidative stress biomarkers in the placenta. The work aims to clarify mechanisms by which early-life pesticide exposure might influence pregnancy outcomes and long-term disease risk.

papers.title: Subtractive Genomic Approach for Identification of Pathogen-Specific Essential Genes as Target and Drug Repurposing in Major Foodborne Bacteria.
papers.abstract: Foodborne diseases pose a substantial threat to global public health and economic stability, with bacterial contamination occurring at multiple stages of the food supply chain. The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among foodborne pathogens has further complicated the prevention and treatment of these infections, underscoring the urgent need for novel, pathogen-specific therapeutic targets. In this study, a comprehensive subtractive genomics approach was employed to systematically identify bacterial key genes (bKGs) as drug targets and to explore corresponding potential therape
papers.summary: This study uses a subtractive genomics pipeline to identify essential genes in major foodborne bacterial pathogens that are absent from the human host, yielding candidate pathogen-specific drug targets. The authors then pair these targets with drug repurposing to propose existing compounds as potential treatments against antimicrobial-resistant foodborne infections. The work is a computational target-discovery exercise that would require experimental validation before clinical relevance.

papers.title: In silico analysis toward functional genomic profiling and bioprospecting Serratia rubidaea VITVS26 for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant potential.
papers.abstract: Proteases from bacteria and their secondary metabolites have bioactivity which can be utilized in therapeutical industries to overcome the negative effects of existing conventional medicines.
papers.summary: This study performed an in silico genomic analysis of Serratia rubidaea VITVS26 to identify genes and biosynthetic pathways linked to anti-inflammatory and antioxidant potential, supporting its bioprospecting as a source of therapeutic proteases and secondary metabolites. The work is computational and predictive, offering a genomic rationale for further experimental validation rather than direct biochemical or clinical evidence.

papers.title: Identification and structural characterization of MMP1 and MMP9 as potential targets of curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a major subtype of lung cancer characterized by substantial molecular heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Curcumin and resveratrol are naturally occurring bioactive compounds with reported anticancer activities, but their potential molecular targets and mechanisms in LUAD remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses computational approaches to identify MMP1 and MMP9 as potential molecular targets of the natural compounds curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma, then characterizes the structural basis of these interactions. The work suggests a mechanistic rationale for the reported anticancer effects of these polyphenols in LUAD, though experimental validation appears limited.

papers.title: Exploring the SWEET gene family and its role in root system architecture in Populus tomentosa.
papers.abstract: Sugars Will Eventually be Exported Transporters (SWEETs) facilitate sugar translocation and shape plant organ development, yet few studies have characterized their functions in root-related physiological processes in woody perennials.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the SWEET sugar transporter gene family in the woody perennial Populus tomentosa and investigates its role in root system architecture. It provides a family-wide survey and links specific SWEET genes to root development traits in a tree species, extending knowledge from model herbaceous plants to woody perennials.

papers.title: Genome-wide association study of growth-related traits in mandarin fish (Siniperca chuatsi): identification of cross-trait associated loci and candidate genes using single-trait and multivariate linear mixed models.
papers.abstract: Mandarin fish (S. chuatsi) is China's most economically important freshwater aquaculture species, yet selective breeding remains constrained by long generation intervals and limited genomic resources. We performed whole-genome resequencing of 98 Siniperca chuatsi individuals (minimum 10-fold coverage), retaining 1,310,398 quality-controlled bi-allelic SNPs across 24 chromosomes. Population structure analysis (principal component analysis, neighbor-joining, and ADMIXTURE) resolved four primary ancestral lineages that further separated into up to six finer-scale ancestry components, with evidenc
papers.summary: This study performed whole-genome resequencing of 98 mandarin fish to identify 1.3 million SNPs and used both single-trait and multivariate linear mixed models to find genetic loci associated with growth-related traits. The authors identified cross-trait associated loci and candidate genes, and resolved population structure into four to six ancestral lineages. This provides genomic resources to support selective breeding in an economically important aquaculture species.

papers.title: Epigenetic modification of neurotransmitter pathways during fasting: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Dietary restriction, encompassing intermittent fasting and caloric restriction, represents a prominent non-pharmacological approach to modulating brain aging and neuronal resilience. Emerging evidence links metabolism to long-term neural plasticity through epigenetic mechanisms, yet findings remain fragmented. This review integrates preclinical evidence on how dietary restriction alters brain epigenetic regulation and links these changes to neurocognitive outcomes.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes preclinical evidence on how dietary restriction (intermittent fasting and caloric restriction) alters brain epigenetic regulation, particularly within neurotransmitter pathways, and connects these changes to neurocognitive outcomes. It argues that metabolism can influence long-term neural plasticity through epigenetic mechanisms, though the existing findings are fragmented. The review aims to integrate this scattered literature into a coherent picture linking diet, epigenetics, and brain aging.

papers.title: Discriminating malignancy of pulmonary nodules using a peripheral blood leukocyte DNA methylation-based SEMO network model.
papers.abstract: Accurately discriminating malignant pulmonary nodules from benign lesions remains challenging, particularly in subcentimeter lesions. This study developed and internally validated a peripheral blood leukocyte (PBL) DNA methylation-derived Selective Epigenomic Module Optimization (SEMO) network model to improve risk stratification.
papers.summary: This study developed a model based on DNA methylation patterns in peripheral blood leukocytes, using a network approach called SEMO (Selective Epigenomic Module Optimization), to distinguish malignant pulmonary nodules from benign ones. The model was developed and internally validated, with the aim of improving risk stratification, especially for nodules smaller than one centimeter where discrimination is particularly difficult.
